{{Short description|Element of algebraic structure}}
{{More citations needed|date=January 2023}}
In [[mathematics]], a '''Garside element''' is an element of an [[algebraic structure]] such as a [[monoid]] that has several desirable properties.

Formally, if ''M'' is a monoid, then an element &Delta; of ''M'' is said to be a '''Garside element''' if the set of all right divisors of &Delta;,
:<math>\{ r \in M \mid \text{for some } x \in M, \Delta = x r \},</math>
is the same set as the set of all left divisors of &Delta;,
:<math>\{ \ell \in M \mid \text{for some } x \in M, \Delta = \ell x \},</math>
and this set [[generating set|generates]] ''M''.

A Garside element is in general not unique: any power of a Garside element is again a Garside element.

== Garside monoid and Garside group ==
A '''Garside monoid''' is a monoid with the following properties:
* Finitely generated and atomic;
* [[Cancellative]];
* The [[Partially ordered set|partial order]] relations of divisibility are [[Lattice (order)|lattices]];
* There exists a Garside element.

A Garside monoid satisfies the [[Ore condition for multiplicative sets]] and hence embeds in its group of fractions: such a group is a '''Garside group'''. A Garside group is [[biautomatic group|biautomatic]] and hence has solvable [[Word problem for groups|word problem]] and [[conjugacy problem]]. Examples of such groups include [[braid group]]s and, more generally, [[Artin group]]s of [[Artin group of finite type|finite Coxeter type]].<ref name=dehorneyparis>{{citation | last1=Dehornoy | first1=Patrick | author1-link=Patrick Dehornoy |last2=Paris | first2=Luis | title=Gaussian groups and Garside groups, two generalisations of Artin groups | journal=[[Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society]] | volume=79 | number=3 | pages=569–604 | year=1999 | doi=10.1112/s0024611599012071| citeseerx=10.1.1.595.739 | s2cid=5254961 }}</ref>

The name was coined by [[Patrick Dehornoy]] and Luis Paris<ref name=dehorneyparis/> to mark the work on the conjugacy problem for braid groups of Frank Arnold Garside (1915–1988), a teacher at [[Magdalen College School, Oxford]] who served as [[List of mayors of Oxford|Lord Mayor of Oxford]] in 1984–1985.<ref>{{citation | last=Garside | first=Frank A. | title=The braid group and other groups | journal=Quarterly Journal of Mathematics |series=Second Series | volume=20 | pages=235–254 | year=1969 | doi=10.1093/qmath/20.1.235| bibcode=1969QJMat..20..235G | doi-access=free }}</ref>
